scope: Selected owned artworks; editorial exhibition, not an artist-declared grouping

findings: W001 anchor image confirms: the head has two yellow-pupiled eyes with pink lash-like marks, a translucent layered face on a deep red ground, a gold-outlined tooth row at the bottom, and black silhouette figures at lower right — not a 'black silhouette with a raised finger and a pointed horn-like protrusion along the right edge' as described; the black shapes are at the lower portion, not the right edge. The whyHere and observations are broadly accurate but the 'barely contains pooling color patches' phrasing is supportable.

W034 anchor image confirms: the face has two large circular eye sockets each ringed with jagged crown-like black spikes and containing layered marks; the background is a warm brown-gray; there is no clear 'vertical color divide' splitting the head into pale olive-brown left and darker gray right halves — the left eye area is more olive-yellow and the right socket is darker but this is not a clean vertical stripe. The whyHere claim of 'vertical color divide' overstates what is visible; corrected to reference the asymmetric eye sockets and dense scrawl.

W061 anchor image confirms: both eyes are large spiral-like sockets with red marks; the left eye is not simply 'deeper and more hollowed' — both eyes are prominent and heavily marked with red-orange scrawl; the 'pinpoint of light' in the right eye is not clearly visible at this resolution. The orange-red drop at the chin is confirmed. Transition and whyHere corrected to avoid unsupported detail about a 'pinpoint of light.'

W047 (magenta field): the image shows a magenta background with loosely drawn black outlines forming a face; the face marks are sparse and gestural rather than 'dense black strokes' that 'pile up so thickly they read as shadow and mass.' The whyHere overstates the density; corrected to reflect the loose, open quality of the marks against the saturated ground.

W010 has no face — it is an abstract composition of nested rectangles and bands. Its placement in Chapter 3 as a transition from banded faces to pure geometry is valid and honest. The whyHere correctly notes 'no face at all.'

W048 does not clearly show 'thick black borders that stack and lean like crates' — it shows angular geometric forms with a red-and-white spiral and a zigzag band. The 'crates' metaphor is an invented object; corrected to describe visible angular outlines and the spiral.

Chapter 5 ('The Ring, the Split, the Stare') contains only one stop (W058) after the removal of W047 and W061 duplicates. A single-stop chapter is structurally weak. W047 and W061 were already placed in Chapter 1. To resolve this, W058 is moved to close Chapter 4 as a final ornament/boundary work, and Chapter 5 is dissolved. Chapter 4 is retitled to accommodate this. This keeps all 20 slots placed exactly once and produces 4 chapters of reasonable depth.
The introduction claims 'Twenty works' — this is accurate for the membership count and acceptable as visitor prose since it describes the exhibition size, not a technical parameter.

W030 transition references 'W001's outline is soft and translucent' in the original but the corrected transition should reference the immediately preceding work W047, not W001. Checked: the draft transition for W030 correctly references the magenta field of the preceding W047. This is fine.
W034 whyHere removed unsupported 'vertical color divide' claim; replaced with reference to the asymmetric, heavily ringed eye sockets visible in the anchor image.
W061 whyHere removed unsupported 'pinpoint of light' claim; replaced with reference to the red-orange scrawl filling both eye sockets and the confirmed red drop at the chin.
W047 whyHere corrected: marks are gestural and open against the magenta ground, not densely piled. The flat confrontational quality is still supportable.
W048 whyHere: 'crates' metaphor removed; replaced with description of angular overlapping outlines and the red spiral anchor.
Repetitive language audit: 'festive and unsettling' appears in both W051 and W054 whyHere text — corrected W054 to use different phrasing.
Chapter 5 dissolved; W058 moved to end of Chapter 4 as closing stop. Chapter 4 retitled to reflect the expanded scope (skulls, ornaments, and the enclosing ring).
All 20 slots confirmed present exactly once in the revised gallery.

evidence.limitation: Ensemble sheet review and three original anchors; not full-resolution individual inspection of every work or a visitor study

title: Outline and Interior
question: How do outlines and interior marks take turns directing your attention?
introduction: Follow heads described by open contours into layered faces, geometric divisions and ringed forms. Outlines can separate features, connect them or become a subject of their own. An abstract arrangement of rectangles and bands offers a contrast to the heads around it. Compare what lies inside a boundary with the marks crossing that boundary.
closing: Compare a facial outline with a geometric division elsewhere in the gallery. What does each boundary make easier to distinguish, and what crosses it?

chapters.title: Faces Against Flat Grounds
chapters.introduction: Four heads sit against unbroken, single-color fields. The outline alone separates figure from ground, and interior marks already push toward it.

stops.whyHere: A translucent, layered head floats on an unbroken red field; overlapping color patches and mismatched yellow-pupiled eyes press against a soft outer edge.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #26

stops.whyHere: A heavy black outline holds a head crammed with multicolored scrawl against a clean blue ground; both eye sockets are filled with red-orange marks, and a red drop hangs from the chin.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both heads float on flat single-color grounds, but where the first outline is soft and translucent, this one is a thick black wall barely containing the wiring inside.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #32

stops.whyHere: On a saturated magenta field, loose gestural black marks trace a face with open, sparse lines—the ground itself does the pressing, leaving the marks little room to breathe.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The clean blue ground gives way to an all-over magenta that eliminates any sense of distance, pushing the face forward with nowhere to recede.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #44

stops.whyHere: A head emerges from a hot orange field as flat black fragments and wire-like outlines; a teal X in the eye area reads as something refused or sealed off.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The magenta field is replaced by a warm orange, but the same flatness persists—here the face fragments rather than consolidates, its eye crossed out rather than staring.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #43

chapters.title: Marks That Multiply
chapters.introduction: Works where interior marks layer so densely that the accumulation itself becomes a second boundary—a structure built from repeated scribble rather than a single drawn line.

stops.whyHere: Yellow loops, teal tangles, and a jaw broken open by sharp white teeth build a head that vibrates against its still purple ground.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Moving from a fragmented orange face to a purple ground, the marks here multiply into a dense crown that feels like a shout caught mid-release.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #46

stops.whyHere: Dense interior hatching makes this animal-like head feel caged inside its own lines; teal peeks through gaps in the black scaffolding.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works pile marks until the face feels trapped inside them, but where the previous erupts upward, this one turns inward, its whisker-lines pressing against the frame.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #56

stops.whyHere: Jagged white teeth appear everywhere—around eyes, across the brow, lining the mouth—so the whole head reads as a structure built from biting.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The animal silhouette gives way to a more frontal face, but the tooth motif spreads from mouth to every border, turning the whole surface into a biting edge.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #5

stops.whyHere: The face splits almost down its center—yellow and blue marks flood the left, red and teal claim the right—holding two distinct mark-fields in one skull.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous work repeats one motif across the whole face, this head divides itself, its dense marks segregated into two competing halves.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #53

stops.whyHere: Thick black scrawl surrounds a face whose two large eye sockets, each ringed with jagged crown-like spikes, stare out from an asymmetric, heavily worked skull.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The split face is replaced by one that feels compressed from all sides, its scrawl so dense the head seems to be shrinking under its own marks.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #54

chapters.title: Frames Within Faces
chapters.introduction: Works where a geometric element—rectangle, grid, nested box, or band—appears inside or around the face, adding a second, harder layer of enclosure to the drawn outline.

stops.whyHere: A skull sits frontal on saturated blue; eye circles contain layered spirals and grids, and a dark grid of thin lines crosses the upper background.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The compressed, scrawled face opens onto a bright blue field, but the skull's eye sockets now contain their own internal grids—enclosure folded inside enclosure.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #59

stops.whyHere: A rectangular barred socket at the face's center suggests something sealed behind the surface; gold teeth flash against a dark mouth cavity like ornament and lock at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous work's grids sit inside the eyes, here a single barred rectangle dominates the face's center, reading unmistakably as a window with bars.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #50

stops.whyHere: Yellow banding runs across chin, cheeks, and forehead, striping the face like a crate; two eyes carry different internal marks—zigzag versus cross—lending asymmetric unease.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The barred socket gives way to horizontal banding that wraps the whole face, turning the head into a striped, boxed form.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #40

stops.whyHere: Teal bars stack along one edge while vertical stripes press the other; crossed-out eyes and a red triangle crown give the boxed-in head a confrontational charge.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Both works use banding to press the face inward, but here the bands migrate to the margins, squeezing the head from outside rather than marking it from within.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #4

stops.whyHere: Concentric nested rectangles pull the eye toward a tight spiral at the center; sawtooth lines slice across the surface, with barely any negative space surviving—no face, only frame.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The banded face gives way to a composition where the frame is the entire subject—nested rectangles with no face at all, containment stripped to its purest geometry.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #1

stops.whyHere: Angular overlapping outlines lean and collide across the surface; a red-and-white spiral anchors the upper center while a zigzag band cuts the lower third, resisting any single focal point.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The concentric inward pull of the previous work is answered here by angular outlines that lean and collide, replacing centered compression with a restless, multi-directional push.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #2

chapters.title: Skulls With Added Weight
chapters.introduction: Skull forms carrying chains, visors, medallions, or a white ring. Each addition sits visibly on the form, making the boundary a physical object rather than a drawn edge.

stops.whyHere: Red dashes burst outward behind the skull like a broadcast signal; teeth ring the eye sockets as well as the jaw, multiplying mouths across the whole face.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Moving from abstract boxes back to a face, this skull radiates outward—the first work in the exhibition where the boundary seems to be pushing energy away rather than holding it in.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #25

stops.whyHere: A chain and medallion pull the skull rightward; radiating color bands fan behind it, making the form feel ornamental and hollow at once.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous skull broadcasts outward through red dashes, this one is weighted down by a chain, its outward radiation replaced by decorative gravity.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #24

stops.whyHere: Rectangular goggle-like eye shapes give the skull a mask quality; cyan and yellow patches leak through black scaffolding, giving the form an unstable, lit-from-within appearance.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The chain of the previous work adds external weight; here the skull's own eye sockets become rigid rectangular frames, containment built into the anatomy itself.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #48

stops.whyHere: An oversized pink visor turns eyewear into a grinning mouth-border; a small dripping form at the jaw suggests something leaking out of an otherwise sealed figure.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: Where the previous skull's rectangular eyes are hollow and stiff, this visor is pink and tooth-rimmed, transforming a protective object into a boundary that grins back.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #16

stops.whyHere: A heavy white ring frames a face staring through mismatched eyes—one ringed in yellow-green spikes, the other a tight spiral; all pattern density is concentrated inside the circle, the surrounding field left sparse.
stops.transitionFromPrevious: The visor of the previous work is a partial frame; here a complete white ring encloses the entire face, making the boundary a deliberate, visible object and closing the exhibition's central question in plain sight.
stops.title: nnxyz rawblocks #31
